text:
priya: FYI rolling BMC NIC firmware to ap-south1 just flipped something — out-of-band consoles for ~12 racks are flapping and provisioning is piling up. seeing a big queue on the provisioner.
sam: can you paste the oob logs? is this the secure-boot toggle change?
priya: quick dump below — it's the 1.4.2 -> 1.5.0 rollout that enabled stricter uefi attr handling. not explicitly toggling secure boot, but we see oob sessions drop with netlink errors.
priya: ```
2026-03-20T09:02:11Z bmc-238 kernel: r8152 1-1.2 eth0: link down
2026-03-20T09:02:12Z oob-daemon[4217]: session reset: netlink: failed to set attr 0x4
2026-03-20T09:02:13Z provisioner[pid=92]: enqueue host=rack-12-gpu-03 state=awaiting-oob
```
infra-bot: ALERT: oob-console-flap detected in ap-south1 (12 hosts). auto-rate-limit applied to new provisioning requests for 15m.
omar: if sessions are dropping we might be hitting firmware NIC reinitialization on boot. that can spike the DHCP/arp storms and impact the provisioning control plane.
lena: Can we pause the rollout? if 1.5.0 has stricter UEFI parsing it might be toggling secure boot enforcement inadvertently on some firmware combos.
priya: re: pause — I asked release to hold canary 2 -> 3, but can run a full stop if infra approves.
sam: +1 pause. we need to prevent further hosts entering the queue. can we drain the provisioner queue into a holding pool and backfill later? that reduces churn.
omar: suggest immediate mitigation: 1) pause rollout 2) shift new builds to eu1/ue-west to avoid capacity hit in ap-south1 3) run selective BMC rollback on nodes that failed oob health checks.
priya: rollback command we use for OOB is: ```scripts/oob-rollback --hosts @failed-1.5.0 --image 1.4.2 --no-verify```
lena: are we comfortable with automatic rollback? last time we did that it recovered consoles but left some hosts needing manual IP rebind. manual ops will be noisy.
sam: do a two-tier approach: automated rollback for nodes failing 3+ oob reconnects, and manual for intermittent ones. also throttle the provisioner accept rate: set provisioner.max_concurrent_oob to 10.
priya: changing provisioner config now. patch: ```kubectl -n infra set env deployment/provisioner PROV_MAX_OOB=10```
priya: applied. infra-bot: acknowledged config change.
deploy-bot: Canaries halted on rollout 1.5.0 by @release.
omar: next we should run targeted netlink/kernel checks on affected NIC vendor (Realtek r8152) across the fleet. vendor matrix shows older NIC microcode + 1.5.0 had a reg write ordering change.
lena: cost note — if we shift builds to eu1 we have to spin up warm racks; that'll add ~0.12 $/GPU-hour while we backfill. ops OK to trade cost for availability?
priya: finance pinged — better to incur short term region shift costs than SLA breaches. I'm okay.
sam: I'll open a quick runbook: steps to detect, rollback, and mark nodes healthy so provisioner can fast-track. keeping it concise.
sam: runbook snippet: ```1) query oob-health --since=10m --filter=netlink_fail 2) rollback via scripts/oob-rollback 3) re-run oob-health-check 4) mark-provisioner host=XXX state=ready```
priya: doing detection sweep now (reaction :eyes:). will post count.
priya: sweep result: 12 failed consoles, 8 transient (recovered), 4 consistently failing -> queued for rollback.
omar: ok, start rollback on 4. coordinate with oncall for any manual IP fixes.
lena: also add a temporary routing rule on the oob-proxy to increase connection timeouts to 45s; that might mask brief NIC reinitializations and reduce rollbacks.
sam: good idea. command: ```infractl oob-proxy set --connect-timeout 45s --region ap-south1```
priya: applied proxy timeout. infra-bot: proxy config change deployed, 3xx hosts reconnected.
priya: rollback started on 4 hosts. monitoring.
priya: update 09:06 UTC — 3 of 4 rolled back and consoles stable, one host requires manual MAC rebind (oncall pinged). provisioner queue length dropped 60%.
lena: thanks. let's keep rollout paused and run deeper tests on NIC vendor combos before resuming. create a test matrix with r8152 variants + uefi attr flags.
omar: also file an upstream bug with vendor for kernel netlink handling. include logs and regen steps.
sam: I'm posting the runbook and incident notes in #incidents after we finish cleanup. good job team.
priya: filing postmortem draft and test matrix. we'll propose updated rollout canary gating that includes oob-health checks and vendor-microcode matching.
priya: closing thread once all hosts cleared. (reaction :white_check_mark:)
